items.text: In 1923, physical chemists Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted in DenmarkandThomasMartinLowryinEnglandindependently proposed the theory that carries their names. In the BronstedLowry theory,acids and bases are defined by theway they react witheachother

items.label: text
items.text: They defined an acid as a substance that can donate a proton, i.e. a proton donor (hydrogen ion, H+). They defined a base as a substance that can accept a proton,i.e.a proton acceptor.

items.label: text
items.text: In the reverse reaction:

items.label: list_item

items.label: list_item
items.text: Cl-is behaving as a base because it is accepting a proton from HO+.

items.label: text
items.text: When the acid HCl loses a proton it forms a base, Cl-. These two species are called a conjugate acid-base pair.

items.label: text
items.text: When the acid HO+loses a proton it forms the baseHzO. These two species alsoform a conjugate acid-base pair.
